correctness.rationale: The D_m generator Gram matrix is 1+δ_ij. Its polar in R^{m+1} is the star inequality cone C_m with one-dimensional lineality; polarity exchanges Gaussian face dimensions, so J_m has the law of active pooled leaves K_m. The unique threshold T solves T+∑(T−G_i)_+=G_0. Setting u_m by m[φ(u_m)−u_m Φbar(u_m)]=u_m gives u_m²∼2log m by Mills expansions. Threshold comparisons −u_m±epsilon/u_m and binomial counts imply K_m/u_m²→1 in probability. The exceptional-event bound using 6u² pooled leaves, Chernoff and G_0>4u yields second moment E K_m²=O(u_m^4), so normalized means converge. No finite simulations establish these infinite limits.
